products.name: InternLM (Shanghai AI Lab)
products.note: Chinese open-source LLM; academic research; cross-border data review advised

reading.body:
Shanghai AI Laboratory is a government-affiliated research institution in China operating InternLM, an open-source large language model positioned for academic research across Chinese universities and scientific applications.

The laboratory's stated focus spans model capability, embodied robotics, and AI safety frameworks, with recent emphasis on science-oriented systems that integrate language models, specialist agents, and physical automation. This portfolio suggests a research strategy prioritizing broad capability development rather than any single domain constraint. The 2026 announcement of AI-for-science results and a scientific discovery platform indicates the institution is testing large models as infrastructure for experimental workflows, from hypothesis through validation.

What matters for AI infrastructure is that Shanghai AI Laboratory operates within China's university and research ecosystem, not as a commercial infrastructure builder or power provider. The laboratory contributes to model capability and research methodology but does not control the compute, buildings, or power grids that determine how quickly those capabilities can scale. It represents the downstream user of infrastructure, not the constraint that binds it.

The data does not cover the laboratory's budget, its access to compute hardware, or the power requirements of its training and inference systems. Without those facts, the connection between its research ambitions and the infrastructure constraints that may or may not enable them remains unmeasured.

profile_text.body:
Shanghai AI Laboratory is a non-profit, government-run artificial intelligence laboratory in China, according to its own site. It recruits researchers internationally across areas it lists as AI, large models, embodied intelligence, safe and trustworthy AI, AI for Science, basic platforms, the innovation chain and management support, and describes the aim as co-creating an AGI future. Since 2022 it has run a joint doctoral training program with more than ten universities, among them Peking University, Tsinghua University, Fudan University, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Tongji University, the University of Science and Technology of China and Zhejiang University.

The laboratory's tracked product is InternLM, described as a Chinese open-source large language model used in academic research, with cross-border data review advised. Its site reports several releases: an upgraded 书生·端砚 scientific discovery platform presented at the 2026 Pujiang Innovation Forum, with its full-stack services opened, and a 书生 physical world model, W0. It also describes an embodied full-stack engine, Intern-Robotics, and ten joint scientific intelligence results announced with universities, research institutes and industry partners at the 2026 WAIC science frontier forum, covering life sciences, materials science and deep space astronomy. Professor Zhou Bowen is quoted proposing that scientific research is the next programming. The laboratory describes a general-specialty fusion technical system in three layers, an AI-45 degree balance law governing safety and performance over the long term, a causal path toward trustworthy AGI through successive stages of broad alignment, intervenability and reflection, and risk management spanning assessment, training, base, application and verification. It also runs a "North Star" talent plan.

No litigation and no MCP servers are recorded for the laboratory.
